name: Town Center / CBD (Clock Tower)
description: The compact commercial core around the landmark clock tower packs markets, banks, cafes, coffee houses, guesthouses, and trekking offices into easy walking distance. It is the most convenient base for arranging climbs and safaris, and the busiest, liveliest part of a generally quiet town.
bestFor: Convenience seekers, first-timers, trekkers arranging expeditions
pros: Best cafes, coffee houses, and wifi options
Easy to book treks and transport
cons: Busier and dustier than uphill areas

name: Shanty Town (Uphill Residential)
tagline: Leafy, quiet, and a little cooler
description: Despite the name, this uphill residential area is Moshi's greener, calmer side, with leafy streets, older houses, and a slower pace. It sits a short ride above the center, offering a more settled feel for longer stays while remaining close to town amenities.
bestFor: Slow travelers and longer stays wanting quiet
pros: Quieter and greener than the CBD

name: Marangu Road / Kilimanjaro Gate
tagline: Toward the mountain and its gateway
description: The road climbing toward Marangu and the Kilimanjaro national park gate runs through lush, higher-elevation villages, banana and coffee shambas, and lodges catering to trekkers. It is greener, cooler, and closer to the trailheads, trading town convenience for scenery and proximity to the climb.
bestFor: Climbers and nature lovers wanting to be near the gate
pros: Closest feel to the mountain and trailheads

name: Machame / Coffee-Farm Slopes
description: The Machame area on Kilimanjaro's southwestern slopes is classic Chagga coffee country, a patchwork of small farms, forest, and villages that also serves as a popular Kilimanjaro trekking route start. It is greener, higher, and more rural than Moshi, ideal for immersion in local farm life.
bestFor: Coffee lovers and immersion-minded slow travelers
pros: Access to the Machame trekking route
